label: E-9: maximum continuous employment activity period
appliesTo: Employment Permit System workers on E-9
why: Known universally as the four-year-ten-month visa, and routinely misread as a lifetime ceiling on working in Korea. It is a limit on one continuous period: a worker meeting the conditions can leave and return under the re-entry special case, and separately can move to E-7-4 skilled status without the cycle at all. Presenting it as a hard end date makes people plan a departure they may not need.

history.source: Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers — employment activity period and extension
history.note: An initial employment activity period plus an extension, commonly totalling 4 years and 10 months of continuous work. Not an absolute lifetime cap: long-serving workers meeting the conditions can re-enter on E-9 under the re-entry special case after a short period outside Korea, currently one month.
